ultraloot.guide.automation.1: Ultra Loot uses the standard NeoForge capabilities, so cables and pipes from other tech mods connect directly: FE cables to Energy Input faces, item pipes to Item Output faces, XP fluid pipes to XP Input faces.
ultraloot.guide.automation.1.title: Cables and pipes
ultraloot.guide.automation.2: Machines work while their chunk is loaded and ticking. They never load chunks by themselves. When the chunk unloads they pause; progress, energy, XP, items and statistics are saved and resume later.
ultraloot.guide.automation.2.title: Chunks
ultraloot.guide.automation.3: Breaking a machine drops its cards and items, and releases stored XP as orbs. Stored FE is lost, so empty the buffer first if it matters.
ultraloot.guide.automation.3.title: Moving a machine
ultraloot.guide.components.1: Every machine starts from a §lMachine Frame§r and a §lLogic Circuit§r. Make these first; they only need iron, glass, copper and redstone.
ultraloot.guide.components.1.title: Machine Frame
ultraloot.guide.components.2: Logic Circuits come in pairs. Better circuits gate the higher tiers: Enhanced (Tier II), Refined (Tier III) and Stellar (Tier IV).
ultraloot.guide.components.2.title: Logic Circuit
ultraloot.guide.components.3: The §lLoot Core§r is the heart of a Loot Generator.
ultraloot.guide.components.3.title: Loot Core
ultraloot.guide.components.4: The §lSoul Core§r is the heart of a Mob Loot Generator.
ultraloot.guide.components.4.title: Soul Core
ultraloot.guide.components.5: Machines need §lForge Energy (FE)§r. Ultra Loot does not make power: use any generator from another tech mod and connect its cable to an §lEnergy Input§r face (back and bottom by default).
ultraloot.guide.components.5.title: Power
ultraloot.guide.energy.1:
FE buffer by tier: 10,000 / 25,000 / 50,000 / 100,000. Max input per transfer: 250 / 625 / 1,250 / 2,500.

An operation is paid in one piece. If a card stack costs more than the tier's buffer, the buffer §lgrows§r to hold one operation, so you are never blocked by buffer size. Stored FE is never thrown away when it shrinks back.
ultraloot.guide.energy.1.title: FE buffer
ultraloot.guide.energy.2: Higher tiers are §lnever less efficient§r: FE per roll or kill only goes down as the tier goes up, while speed and work per operation go up. One Tier IV machine always beats several Tier I machines on energy.
ultraloot.guide.energy.2.title: Efficiency by tier
ultraloot.guide.energy.3: The XP tank does §lnot§r grow. An expensive mob with a Quantity Card can need more XP per operation than a Tier I tank holds; the machine then shows §lCost exceeds XP tank§r in red. Remove the Quantity Card or use a higher tier.
ultraloot.guide.energy.3.title: The XP limit
ultraloot.guide.experience.1: The Mob Loot Generator stores experience as §lpoints§r in a tank. The tank can only be filled, never drained by automation, and the machine never takes XP from players on its own.
ultraloot.guide.experience.1.title: The XP tank
ultraloot.guide.experience.2:
Ways to fill it:
- §lBottles o' Enchanting§r in the XP slot (7 points each)
- an §lExperience Capsule§r
- XP fluids from other mods (tag c:experience, 20 mB = 1 point) through an XP Input face
- a §lRange Card§r, which absorbs XP orbs around the machine
ultraloot.guide.experience.2.title: Filling the tank
ultraloot.guide.experience.3: Sneak and use the §lExperience Capsule§r to store your own XP in it, up to 30 levels (1,395 points). Put the full capsule in the machine's XP slot; the empty capsule comes back and can be pulled out by a hopper.
ultraloot.guide.experience.3.title: Experience Capsule
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.1: Place it, put chests or barrels within range and give it FE. Each operation rolls the selected §lloot profile§r and puts the result straight into those inventories. It has no inventory of its own and never drops items.
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.1.title: How it works
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.2:
Tier I to IV:
- rolls per operation: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4
- scan range: 5 / 8 / 12 / 16 blocks
- FE per roll: 800 / 720 / 640 / 560
- speed: 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 3x

A base cycle takes 10 seconds at 1x.
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.2.title: Tiers
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.3:
Every 5 seconds the machine scans the loaded block entities in range. The §lInventory Scan§r tab lists every inventory it found, its distance and free slots.

An inventory that §ltouches§r the machine is only used if that face is set to §lItem Target§r, so loot never goes into a battery behind its energy face.
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.3.title: Finding inventories
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.4:
Before paying, the machine §lsimulates§r the whole delivery. Items are spread round robin across targets. Only when everything fits is the loot inserted and the FE paid. If not, nothing is generated, nothing is consumed and the status says §lInventories are full§r.

Nothing is ever lost or duplicated.
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.4.title: Safe delivery
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.5: Upgrade a machine by crafting it again with the previous tier in the centre: Tier II needs gold, diamonds and an Enhanced Circuit; Tier III emeralds, netherite and a Refined Circuit; Tier IV shulker shells, diamond blocks, a nether star and a Stellar Circuit.
ultraloot.guide.loot_generator.5.title: Upgrading the tier
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.1: Craft a §lBlank Mob Card§r and use it on a living mob. The mob is not hurt; the card now carries that mob. Bosses, blacklisted mobs and mobs whose loot cannot be found cannot be imprinted.
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.1.title: Imprinting a mob
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.2: Mobs have §lreward tiers§r. Tier I (chicken, zombie, skeleton...) is cheap. Tier II (cow, blaze, enderman...) costs more. Tier III (witch, evoker, shulker...) costs the most FE and XP per kill. The card tooltip shows the tier, XP per kill and FE cost.
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.2.title: Mob tiers
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.3: Card data §lwears out§r with use: every simulated kill adds 1 wear. A card stays intact for 2,048 kills. Over the next 1,024 kills it decays: each kill has a growing chance to give §lRotten Flesh§r instead of loot, and the FE cost rises up to double.
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.3.title: Card wear
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.4: A fully §lcorrupted§r card still runs, but only makes Rotten Flesh at double FE. It never breaks or disappears. Watch the durability bar (green, amber, red) or the §lintegrity§r row in the Mob Configuration tab, and repair the card in a §lCard Restorer§r.
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.4.title: Corrupted cards
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.5: Insert the card by hand in the §lMob Configuration§r tab, or let automation insert it through an §lXP Input§r face while the card slot is empty. Automation can never take the card out. Swapping the card resets the progress bar.
ultraloot.guide.mob_cards.5.title: Inserting a card
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.1: Insert a §lMob Card§r, feed it FE and experience, and it simulates kills of that mob using the mob's own loot table. The drops go to a 27-slot output. No entity is ever spawned, so there is no lag and no mob farm.
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.1.title: How it works
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.2:
Tier I to IV:
- kills per operation: 1 / 1 / 2 / 2
- FE per kill: 1,200 / 1,080 / 960 / 840
- XP tank: 1,000 / 4,000 / 12,000 / 40,000 points
- speed: 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 3x

A base cycle takes 15 seconds at 1x. Each kill also costs the mob's XP price.
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.2.title: Tiers
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.3: Every operation follows the same safe order: check the card, the XP and the FE, simulate the kills, check that all drops fit in the output, and only then commit everything. If anything fails, §lnothing is consumed§r and the card does not wear.
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.3.title: Nothing is wasted
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.4: Take drops by hand in the §lInventory§r tab, let an §lItem Output§r face push them into a chest every half second, or pull them with pipes. All of these work at the same time.
ultraloot.guide.mob_generator.4.title: Getting the drops out
ultraloot.guide.profiles.1: A §lloot profile§r is a loot table plus the context it needs. Choose one in the §lLoot Configuration§r tab. Ultra Loot ships 66 profiles: every vanilla chest, fishing, archaeology, piglin bartering and a few of its own.
ultraloot.guide.profiles.1.title: Choosing a profile
ultraloot.guide.profiles.2: Each profile has a §lminimum tier§r and an §lenergy multiplier§r: valuable tables (End City, Ancient City...) need a better machine and cost more FE per roll. A locked profile shows §lProfile needs a higher tier§r.
ultraloot.guide.profiles.2.title: Tiers and cost
ultraloot.guide.profiles.3: Chest loot tables added by §lother mods§r are discovered automatically. They need a Tier II machine and cost 1.67x energy. Tables that create exploration maps are skipped, because they would search the world for structures and lag the server.
ultraloot.guide.profiles.3.title: Modded loot
ultraloot.guide.profiles.4: With any §lLoot Card§r installed, an output §lfilter§r unlocks: All, Resources, Food or Equipment. Filtered items are destroyed before they exist and counted in the Statistics tab. Filters cannot make a table drop something it doesn't.
ultraloot.guide.profiles.4.title: Filters
ultraloot.guide.received: You received the Ultra Loot Guide. Use it to learn the mod.
ultraloot.guide.recipe_missing: Recipe not available on this server
ultraloot.guide.restorer.1: The §lCard Restorer§r repairs worn Mob Cards with FE. Put a worn card in the input slot and power the block. When the card reaches 0 wear it moves to the output slot and works like new.
ultraloot.guide.restorer.1.title: Repairing cards
ultraloot.guide.restorer.2:
It repairs up to 8 wear points per tick. Each point costs 40 FE times the mob's energy multiplier, and FE is only spent on points actually repaired. A fully corrupted zombie card costs 73,728 FE to restore.

Buffer: 50,000 FE. Input: up to 1,000 FE per transfer.
ultraloot.guide.restorer.2.title: Cost
ultraloot.guide.restorer.3: Every face accepts FE. Hoppers and pipes can insert bound Mob Cards into the input and extract repaired cards from the output, so a restorer can sit in an automatic card loop.
ultraloot.guide.restorer.3.title: Automation
ultraloot.guide.sides.1: Each of the six faces has a role, set in the §lSide Configuration§r tab. Faces are relative to the machine's front, so the setup keeps working however you place it. Left-click a face for the next role, right-click for the previous one.
ultraloot.guide.sides.1.title: Faces
ultraloot.guide.sides.2:
Roles:
- §lEnergy Input§r: accepts FE
- §lItem Target§r (Loot): an inventory touching this face may receive loot
- §lXP Input§r (Mob): XP, XP fluids, bottles, capsules and Mob Cards
- §lItem Output§r (Mob): pushes drops out; pipes may extract
- §lNone§r: nothing connects
ultraloot.guide.sides.2.title: Roles
ultraloot.guide.sides.3:
Defaults. Loot Generator: back and bottom take energy, every other face is an Item Target. Mob Loot Generator: back takes energy, left and top take XP, bottom outputs items.

Upgrade slots are never reachable by automation, and the output can only be extracted, never filled.
ultraloot.guide.sides.3.title: Defaults and safety
ultraloot.guide.title: Ultra Loot Guide
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.1:
Amber (waiting):
- §lNot enough energy§r: add FE or an Efficiency Card
- §lNot enough experience§r: fill the XP tank
- §lInventories are full§r / §lOutput is full§r: empty the chests or the output

The machine resumes by itself once the cause is gone.
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.1.title: Amber statuses
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.2:
Red (your action):
- §lNo inventories in range§r: place a chest in range or set a face to Item Target
- §lProfile needs a higher tier§r: upgrade the machine
- §lCost exceeds XP tank§r: remove the Quantity Card
- §lNo loot table for this mob§r: the tooltip says why (usually a datapack names a missing table)
- §lThis mob cannot be simulated§r: use another mob
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.2.title: Red statuses
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.3: When the status text is too long for the panel, hover it to read it in full. The §lStatistics§r tab counts operations, items made, items filtered, energy and XP used, which helps you compare setups.
ultraloot.guide.troubleshooting.3.title: More help
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.1: Each machine has §lfive upgrade slots§r, one per category: Speed, Quantity, Range, Efficiency and Loot. Each card has levels I to III. Shift-clicking a higher level swaps it in and gives back the old card.
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.1.title: Five slots
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.2:
§lSpeed§r: 1.25x / 1.5x / 2x faster.
§lQuantity§r: 2x / 3x / 4x rolls or kills, each one independent.
§lRange§r: +8 / +16 / +24 scan blocks (Loot), or collects XP orbs within 2 / 4 / 6 blocks (Mob).
§lEfficiency§r: -10% / -20% / -35% energy.
§lLoot§r: +1 / +2 / +3 luck (Loot) or Looting I-III (Mob), and unlocks filters.
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.2.title: What they do
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.3:
Every card except Efficiency raises the energy cost. The final cost per operation is shown in the Overview tab. It is never below 25% of the tier's base cost, so operations are never free.

Levels II and III are crafted from the previous level with better materials and an Enhanced or Refined Circuit.
ultraloot.guide.upgrades.3.title: Energy cost
ultraloot.guide.welcome.1:
§lUltra Loot§r turns energy (FE) into loot. Two machine families do the work:

§1Loot Generator§r: rolls chest, fishing and archaeology loot tables straight into your chests.

§1Mob Loot Generator§r: simulates mob kills from a Mob Card, paid with FE and experience. No mob is ever spawned.
ultraloot.guide.welcome.1.title: What is Ultra Loot?
ultraloot.guide.welcome.2:
Both families come in §lfour tiers§r. Higher tiers are faster, do more per operation, hold more energy and never cost more FE per result.

Every machine has a status line. Its colour and symbol always tell you what to do: cyan square = working, gray square = idle, amber ! = waiting for something, red x = needs your action.
ultraloot.guide.welcome.2.title: Tiers and status
ultraloot.guide.welcome.3:
Use the chapter list on the left, or:

- arrow keys / mouse wheel: turn pages
- click a chapter in the list to jump to it
- hover an item to see its name and tooltip

Craft another copy of this guide from a Book and a Redstone Dust.
